properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-09-13, thinking out loud. Nothing here is intent and nothing should be built from it without his word.

THE IDEA, in his words: templates that seed a design and use modern design practice for a given domain — "almost like a cookie-cutter in a python project" (https://cookiecutter.readthedocs.io/en/stable/). A software project's template would already describe and seed the graph with current software design practice. More templates follow for more domains, each carrying that field's practices, standards, codes and regulations. The invocation shape he sketched is `/genesis + template_x`.

⭐ THE MOTIVATION IS THE PART TO KEEP: "I feel like this would be helpful where somebody is designing in a domain that they are not the expert in." That is a different user from the one reflow2 has been built for so far. Every guided path here assumes the person knows their field and needs help keeping the design coherent; this assumes the opposite, and asks reflow2 to supply the field's shape as well as the discipline.

EXPLICITLY NOT MANDATORY, and he said so unprompted: the standard genesis path stays, and a template is an option for well-defined domains rather than a new front door.

WHAT A TEMPLATE MIGHT CARRY — not settled, and the options differ a lot in ambition:
 · the SHAPE only — the component tiers, the interface classes, the verification kinds a field expects, with nothing filled in
 · the shape plus the QUESTIONS that field always asks, seeded as open gaps rather than as answers
 · the shape plus stated STANDARDS and regulations as Constraints or DesignRules
 · pre-drawn golden thread, so a seeded design is already traceable before anybody types

THREE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea rather than used to argue it down:

 🛑 A TEMPLATE THAT ENCODES "LATEST PRACTICE" GOES STALE, AND A STALE TEMPLATE IS WORSE THAN A BLANK GRAPH — because it carries authority. A newcomer to a domain is exactly the person who cannot tell a current practice from a 2019 one. This is the failure that would sink it, and it is why the authority question is recorded separately.

 🛑 IT COULD PUSH A DESIGN INTO A SHAPE NOBODY CHOSE. reflow2's whole posture is report-don't-judge and intent-moves-only-on-the-owner's-word — certainty is DERIVED from status and provenance precisely so that nothing can forge the user's signature. A seeded design starts full of structure the user never said. Whether that is help or a thumb on the scale depends entirely on how loudly the seeded parts announce themselves.

 🛑 THE SEEDED PARTS COULD BECOME THE DESIGN WITHOUT ANYBODY DECIDING. This project already reads 106 of 108 Components as `planned` and 55 requirements as asserted-awaiting-the-user; a seeded design would arrive with far more of both, and the reports cannot currently tell "seeded by a template" from "somebody wrote this".

⭐ AND THERE IS ALREADY A HOOK FOR THAT LAST ONE, which is the most useful technical observation here: every node carries `provenance` (authored / planned / inferred / healed / reconciled / imported), and requirement certainty is computed from status × provenance. A template would need its own value, or to land as `imported`, so that a seeded requirement can never read as one somebody confirmed. If that is right, the mechanism is mostly present and what is missing is the vocabulary and the seeding path.

WHAT IS NOT ASKED AND SHOULD NOT BE INFERRED: whether reflow2 would SHIP any templates itself, or only accept them. Those are very different products — one makes reflow2 an authority on domains, the other keeps it a tool that carries somebody else's authority.
properties.name: OPEN — should genesis accept a domain SEED TEMPLATE, so somebody designing outside their expertise starts in the field's own shape instead of from a blank graph?
properties.rationale: Captured while @ajs was thinking out loud, as a brainstorm. Recorded as an open question with options rather than a proposal, so a later session does not read it back as a settlement. The counter-arguments sit beside the idea deliberately: an idea killed in conversation loses its reasoning, an idea recorded with its objections keeps both.
